title: Latency-classified socket profiles and SDK priming recipes
creator: Marin Alvarez
description:
Background: Customers are seeing variable tail latency across interactive RPCs (chat/generation) vs background workloads (embeddings/bulk). Current SDK defaults are one-size-fits-all which forces operators to choose either lower latency with higher cost or conservative pooling that increases cold-starts and p95s.

Proposal: Introduce 'latency-classified socket profiles' in all three SDKs (Python/TS/Go). Each profile defines: connection pool size, idle_keepalive_ms, socket_reap_ms, per-request deadline multiplier, priming behavior, and optional speculative hedging settings. SDKs will ship three default profiles: "interactive" (low-latency, aggressive priming), "standard" (balanced), and "background" (cost-optimized).

In addition, provide a lightweight public API: SDK.prime(profile, hints) which allows apps to perform safe, low-cost warmups (small preflight requests with trace headers) to populate connection/KV caches and warm remote sequencing where applicable.

Key behaviors:
- Per-route override: developers can attach a profile per API route (generation vs embeddings).
- Adaptive lease softening: idle sockets may be soft-leased to higher-priority lanes instead of immediate close; this reduces reconnect churn for bursty interactive traffic.
- Hedging: optional single-duplicate speculative request for interactive profile with randomized jitter to shave tail latency; bounded by cost ceiling config.
- Telemetry: new tags on SDK metrics (profile, primed=true/false, hedged=true/false) and per-profile breakdowns on latency/cost dashboards.

Why this is different: Existing tickets focus on transport defaults, keepalive and timeouts individually. This ticket bundles a developer-facing profile abstraction + a safe priming API + cross-language examples and rollout plan so product teams can adopt without bespoke tuning per service.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles implemented and exported in Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs with identical semantic defaults
SDK.prime API implemented and documented with examples for generation and embeddings
Unit tests for profile application, priming flow, and hedging behavior across SDKs
Integration benchmark: p95 reduction >= 8% for interactive profile in synthetic chat benchmark without >5% token cost increase
Dashboards updated: latency-by-profile, priming-uptime, hedging-cost, and per-route connection churn
Canary rollout plan documented and automation for percentage-based rollout available
implementation_notes: Expose env override: REDWOOD_SDK_PROFILE and REDWOOD_SDK_PRIME=true for ops debugging
Priming behavior should send a lightweight 'prime' request type to /v1/prime with minimal token usage and special trace headers to bypass rate-limits for priming runs
Hedging must propagate idempotency header so server can detect and dedupe double-processing where applicable
Keep the feature behind a runtime flag per SDK for a staged release and immediate rollback
Add metrics: sdk.requests_by_profile, sdk.primed_connections, sdk.hedged_requests, sdk.conn_reconnects_per_minute
testing_plan: Synthetic benchmark: 3-phase load profile (steady, burst, cooldown) for generation endpoints using interactive vs standard vs background profiles
Chaos test: kill sockets and observe reconnect rates and median/p95 with and without priming
Cost regression harness: measure token + socket lifecycle cost delta for hedging enabled vs disabled
Integration test against canary runtime that supports /v1/prime to ensure priming payloads do not count against normal quota metrics
Cross-language compatibility tests to ensure identical behavior on profile names and telemetry tags
comments: 2025-02-15 Marin Alvarez: Initial triage and problem statement. Mapped to SDK Transport Stabilization. Raised dependency on ENG-7423 for connection pool insights.
2025-02-16 Jordan Kim: Prototype for Python profile API complete. Dropped default idle_keepalive from 2m to 45s for interactive profile — preliminary perf looks promising in local runs.
2025-02-17 Design review (Aisha Patel): Suggested adding visual affordance in Console for 'primed' status per route and guidance copy to explain cost trade-offs to end users.
2025-02-18 Engineering (Liam O'Connor): Opened draft PR for Python priming path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/8421 — seeking cross-language API agreement.
2025-02-19 PM review (Sofia Martinez): Approved canary rollout plan; requested guardrail to disable hedging automatically if cost delta > 7% during canary.

2025-02-20 Jordan Kim: Ran canary on staging cluster for 48h. Observed p95 drop of ~10% for interactive profile in chat trace set. CPU overhead on clients negligible. Attaching perf summary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/profile-perf
risks: Hedging increases request volume and can amplify downstream load; must be limited per-customer and per-route
Priming may be misused as continuous warmups and increase cost if apps set aggressive priming intervals; need sensible defaults and docs
Cross-language semantics mismatch (deadline multipliers) could create surprising behavior; add strict contract tests
Server-side support required: dedupe for hedged requests; rollout coordination with runtime team is necessary
